post.name: flux-identity
post.content:
#!/bin/sh
# FluxBilling: identity from kernel cmdline (fluxhost= fluxpass=).
# Runs in the live env after install; target is mounted at /mnt.
# root ships LOCKED in the profile above - this profile is readable in the
# live environment and is archived with the install logs, so it must never
# carry a usable password. No fallback either: a missing fluxpass= leaves the
# accounts locked rather than handing out a default published in a public repo.
C=$(cat /proc/cmdline)
zget() { echo "$C" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed -n "s/^$1=//p" | head -n1; }
H=$(zget fluxhost); [ -n "$H" ] || H=fluxserver
P=$(zget fluxpass)
echo "$H" > /mnt/etc/hostname
chroot /mnt /bin/sh -c "id user >/dev/null 2>&1 || useradd -m -c 'Default User' user"
if [ -n "$P" ]; then
  chroot /mnt /bin/sh -c "echo root:$P | chpasswd"
  chroot /mnt /bin/sh -c "echo user:$P | chpasswd"
else
  echo "FLUX: no fluxpass= on the kernel command line - root and user stay LOCKED." >&2
fi
unset P
sed -i 's/^#\?PermitRootLogin.*/PermitRootLogin yes/' /mnt/etc/ssh/sshd_config
chroot /mnt systemctl enable sshd
# The kernel command line reaches the installation logs Agama copies onto the
# target; strip the password out of anything that persists.
find /mnt/var/log -type f 2>/dev/null | while read -r f; do
  sed -i 's/fluxpass=[^[:space:]]*/fluxpass=<redacted>/g' "$f" 2>/dev/null || :
done
